voiceover: Saw an objection online? It's been asked before. On Asked and Answered, paste a tweet, an objection, or a screenshot — or just ask any question about the Christian faith. You get a clear answer — and, where it's known, the skeptic who raised it first, often centuries ago — and where to dig deeper. For two thousand years, the hard questions have been asked — and seriously answered, not dodged. Then there's Study Plans. Instead of endlessly browsing, you get a guided, day-by-day path through the evidence — with a clear finish line, and your progress saved as you go. There are ten guided plans, from beginner to advanced, running fourteen to thirty days — from the thirty-day Resurrection Deep Dive to a twenty-eight-day Debate Prep. And these aren't reading lists. Every day gives you something to do: read the evidence, ask the AI tutor, step into the Debate Arena, then reflect and make it your own. And Reading Clubs: read the great Christian apologists together — chapter by chapter, with discussion questions for each. Six books so far, from C.S. Lewis's Mere Christianity to William Lane Craig's On Guard. Read at your own pace, or work through them with a group. Ask it. Study it. Read it together. Find all three at apologiadaily.com.
